message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most significant and busiest airports across the United States—those that serve as key hubs for domestic travel, international flights, cargo operations, or both:

| Airport (IATA) | City / State | Notable Features |
|-----------------|--------------|------------------|
| **Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International** – ATL | Atlanta, GA | Largest passenger hub worldwide; massive connecting traffic. |
| **Los Angeles International** – LAX | Los Angeles, CA | Major West Coast gateway with extensive international service. |
| **Chicago O’Hare International** – ORD | Chicago, IL | One of the world’s busiest airports; primary Midwest hub. |
| **Dallas/Fort Worth International** – DFW | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | Large U.S. hub with strong domestic network. |
| **Denver International** – DEN | Denver, CO | Fastest-growing airport; central location for cross-country routes. |
| **John F. Kennedy International** – JFK | New York City, NY | Key East Coast entry/exit point for transatlantic flights. |
| **San Francisco International** – SFO | San Francisco, CA | Important West Coast hub especially for Asia-Pacific connections. |
| **Seattle/Tacoma International** – SEA | Seattle, WA | Growing hub on the Pacific Northwest; high tech industry ties. |
| **Miami International** – MIA | Miami, FL | Primary gateway to Latin America & Caribbean destinations. |
| **Orlando International** – ORL | Orlando, FL | Heavy tourist traffic due to theme parks; also serves many charter airlines. |
| **Phoenix Sky Harbor International** – PHX | Phoenix, AZ | Rapidly expanding hub serving Southwest U.S. and Mexico. |
| **Charlotte Douglas International** – CLT | Charlotte, NC | Strong regional presence; growing international services. |
| **Washington Reagan National** – IAD | Washington, DC area | Main federal government access point; heavy business traffic. |
| **Boston Logan International** – BOS | Boston, MA | Northeast hub with robust European links. |

These airports rank among the top in terms of annual passengers, flight movements, and connectivity. They’re often chosen as starting points when planning multi-city itineraries because they offer numerous onward options domestically and internationally.
